# Best 18650 chargers

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL, about $32.90**
- It has four independent bays and takes USB-C with QC3.0 input.
- Charge current is adjustable from 0.25A to 3A.
- The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity, and internal resistance for each cell. It also has capacity grading and storage modes.
- It fits protected 21700 cells and also charges NiMH/NiCd.
- Downsides: LiFePO4 isn't supported. One reviewer found it defaults to the highest current, can end NiMH charges early, and occasionally mistakes NiMH for Li-ion. Watch the first minute of any charge.
- Links: [price and review](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/), [hands-on review](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/)

**Fastest, and best if you use LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4, about $38.95**
- It charges up to 3A in a single slot with a QC input, or 1A each with four cells.
- It supports Li-ion, LiFePO4, and NiMH/NiCd. It also has reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection, an overtime cutoff, and internal-resistance readout.
- Links: [manufacturer page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4), [price and review](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/)

**Budget pick: Tenergy TN270, $18.99**
- It's a simple two-bay wall charger for 18650, 18500, and 14500 Li-ion cells, with reverse-polarity detection and LED status.
- It charges at only 500 mA per slot, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6–7 hours. It has no USB input and no display.
- [Buy at Tenergy](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Also worth a look: Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger**
- Smashing Robotics named it Editor's Choice. It has selectable 500 mA or 1000 mA charging, an LCD, and wide chemistry support, and it has 4.6 stars across 4,608 reviews.
- That ranking comes from an affiliate-based roundup, so weigh it accordingly. I didn't have a direct purchase link, but the [roundup](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/) links to it.

**Which to pick**
- Most people: **XTAR VC4SL**.
- You use LiFePO4 or want maximum speed: **Nitecore UMS4**.
- You just need a cheap charger for one or two flashlight cells: **Tenergy TN270**.

**Safety tips**
- Pick a charger with independent bays and a named termination method (CC/CV for lithium). Avoid no-name units that don't say how they decide a cell is full.
- Use a lower current (0.5A–1A) when you aren't in a hurry, since it's easier on cell life.
- Don't charge lithium cells in a NiMH-only charger, or the reverse.
